A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FSTA/L2Seg research. All 31 pages of v1 and 35 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original L2Seg experiments on CVRP, VRPTW, and CVRPLib, alongside ablations, oracle experiments, prediction analyses, and repeated-seed results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds NDS comparisons, clustered and heterogeneous-demand CVRP evaluations, and an analysis of predictions across search iterations.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a concrete three-hypernode aggregation procedure for 1-VRPPD in Appendix B.1.5 and Table 6; v1 merely names this variant. The core encoder, NAR/AR/SYN decoders, losses, inference procedures, and existing routing adaptations remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds seven-cluster customer distributions and skewed-demand CVRP scenarios at 2k and 5k sizes. This extends distribution coverage within CVRP; the existing uniform CVRP, VRPTW, and CVRPLib evaluations remain. The 1-VRPPD extension is not experimentally evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Neural Deconstruction Search (NDS) comparisons for CVRP and VRPTW at 1k and 2k sizes, with no NDS results at 5k. Existing comparators remain; the new distribution experiments reuse LNS and LKH-3.

E3.justification: New experiments compare in-distribution evaluation with zero-shot transfer under 150s/240s limits and measure adjacent-iteration prediction overlap and segment length over the first ten iterations. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, hyperparameters, and time limits are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled spatial/demand-shift tests and a temporal prediction-stability analysis in Tables 11 and 13. Figure 1 loses its large-capacity stability panel. Existing random-FSTA and feature ablations, oracle experiments, hyperparameter studies, and prediction case studies remain.

E5.justification: The five-independent-seed study and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting in v1 Appendix D.3/Table 11 are retained in v2 Appendix E.4/Table 12, with identical values. No new uncertainty-reporting practice is documented for the added experiments.

E6.justification: Existing L2Seg benchmark scores remain unchanged, while NDS, distribution-shift, and convergence results are added. Table 2 reports NDS at 41.16 versus L2Seg-SYN-L2D at 41.23 on CVRP1k; Table 11 reports zero-shot gains of 0.82%-3.10% over LNS. Section 5.2 also drops v1's claimed minimum 3% advantage over every VRPTW baseline.

T1.justification: v2 adds a finite-lookahead definition of edge stability and a 1-VRPPD feasibility/monotonicity argument in Appendix B.2.4. Earlier proofs are retained. The new extension contains an inconsistency: Table 6's hypernode demands sum to D^k - D^min, whereas the proof assumes net demand D^k.

C1.justification: Both versions claim FSTA formalization, three L2Seg variants, complementary AR/NAR decision-making, broad solver compatibility, and 2x-7x acceleration. The revised abstract and conclusion use an acceleration range already stated in v1's introduction; the central contribution claims remain substantively the same.

C2.justification: Appendix E.6 newly interprets increasing prediction overlap as gradual convergence permitting continued exploration. Appendix E.3 adds interpretation of robustness to spatial and demand shifts. v2 also drops the earlier cash-in-transit variant listing, while retaining the principal synergy explanation and solver-applicability limitation.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the new cluster/demand generation settings and explains rerunning NDS on V100 hardware. It removes v1's asset-license list, CVRPLib access URL, and explicit undirected-DFS label-construction explanation. Existing hyperparameter tables and the promised MIT-licensed GitHub release remain.

R1.justification: New Appendix C.1 substantially expands positioning against LNS, evolutionary algorithms, path decomposition, and L2D, developing explicit arguments about distinctiveness and complementarity beyond v1's brief discussion. References add NDS and Martinovic et al.'s 1-VRPPD work and remove works including Pointer Networks and DeepACO.

P1.justification: Main-text paragraphs are condensed and edited while the six-section organization remains. Appendices gain a contents page and dedicated definitions/comparisons; AR training explanation moves into the main text, implementation subsections are reordered, and reproducibility and LLM-use statements are added.

P2.justification: A different template changes the title/author arrangement, headings, running headers, and display placement throughout. The AR training diagram moves from v1 Figure 10 to v2 Figure 4; Figure 1 loses a panel; Table 6 expands; and Tables 11 and 13 are added. Most earlier displays are retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: The NDS comparison, controlled distribution tests, and temporal stability analysis provide useful additional checks of competitiveness, generalization, and search behavior. These empirical gains support a limited overall improvement. The unchanged core results limit its magnitude, and the new 1-VRPPD load-conservation inconsistency in Table 6 versus Appendix B.2.4 prevents crediting that extension as reliable theoretical strengthening.
